Set them here: who can connect and the password (Access), OSC and MIDI input (Show control), cloud keys and saved-audio limits (Cloud & audio), the default speech model (Models). Test. With the show Safe, run every phrase through the Test bench, say each one on the real channel, and check Activity for "would have fired". Then go through the before-show checklist. Do the move with time to spare Models need internet to download, and voices need each person on comms. Neither can be done five minutes before the house opens.
documents.s: Example: moving a show to the venue machine

documents.t: While Earshot runs, the show lives in show.earshot.json (with a .bak copy) in the host's data folder. That file is not the same as an export: it also holds this computer's settings, cloud keys, link codes and learned voices. Do not hand it to anyone. Use Export show file for a copy that is safe to move. See Data and files.
documents.s: Where the live show is kept

documents.t: Saved secrets: why secrets cannot be read back. When an automation is not running. Privacy.

Earshot keeps every session. The Archive is where you read one back, search what was said, drop markers on the timeline, and export a session for a show report. Every role can read the Archive, search it and export from it. Adding a marker needs an operator or an admin. The mock show "Spring Tour at Harbour Hall". Invented sessions and lines, not a real show.

Every time Earshot starts, it begins a new session. An admin can also start one by hand with New session… under Setup, Show file (see Show files). The list on the left shows sessions newest first. Each has the show's name, its date and start time, and how long it ran. The session that is running now carries a Live now badge. Pick a session to read it. Until you do, the screen says "Pick a session to read it." The header shows its date, start time and length ("so far", for the live one). Lines are listed oldest first, with the time at the right of each line. On a phone the list and the transcript take turns. A back arrow, Back to sessions, returns to the list.

Above the transcript is a row of chips: All channels, then one per channel. Press a channel's chip to show only that channel. Press more chips to add channels. Press All channels to clear them. If nothing matches, the screen says "No lines from these channels in this session." The chips also decide what Export saves: see below.
A long session is loaded a part at a time. Load earlier lines at the top and Load later lines at the bottom page through it.

Type in Search what was said at the top. Results appear as you type. This session searches the session you have open. All sessions searches every session Earshot has kept. Results are headed Search results with a count ("27 matches"). Each shows the channel, the time, the person's name if the line has one, and the line with your words highlighted. Across all sessions, each also says which session it is from. Press a result to open the transcript at that line. Results takes you back to the list of matches, and Back to transcript closes it. If nothing is found: "Nothing matches “your words” in this session." (or "in any session"). Searching the mock show for "standby". Not a real show. How the search reads what you type: You type It finds standby Lines containing the word "standby". Capitals do not matter. lighting cue Lines containing both words, anywhere in the line, in any order. cue 42 Lines containing "cue" and "42". stand Lines containing the word "stand". It does not find "standby": whole words only. Punctuation and symbols are ignored. There are no special search commands. It searches the text as saved, that is, after glossary corrections and number tidying. If the recogniser heard "aleesha" and the glossary changed it to "Alesha", search for Alesha. A line that was translated can also be found by words in its translation. The list shows the best 50 matches. If you expected more, narrow the words or search one session at a time.

A marker is a labelled point on the timeline, like "Act two, cue 42". Markers make a long session easy to find your way around afterwards. To add one (operators and admins, in the session that is live now): Open the live session in the Archive. Find Markers above the transcript (on a narrow screen, press it to open it), and press Add marker. Type the Marker label (up to 120 characters), for example Act one begins. Press Add. The marker is placed at the moment you add it. To use one: under Markers (it shows a count, "Markers (2)"), press a marker to jump to that point in the transcript. A session with none says "No markers in this session." Markers can also be added without touching the Archive: An automation can add one with its Add a marker action, for example a marker for every cue the show caller fires. See Actions. A console can add one over OSC. See OSC addresses.

Export saves the session you are reading as a file. Press it and choose TXT, CSV, JSON or SRT. While it works the screen says, for example, "Preparing CSV…", then "Saved" and the file's name. The mock show's Archive with the Export menu open. Not a real show. The file is named earshot- followed by the session's id, with the format's ending, for example earshot-01KA4T7Q9D5XJ2R8M3N6P0V1WC.csv. If channel chips are on, the export keeps only those channels. The button says how many: "Export (2 ch)". The export is the text as saved: corrected, tidied, and filtered if the channel filters profanity. Typed lines and Earshot's own notices are included, in time order with the speech. warning Times in TXT and CSV files are in UTC, not your local time. On screen, Earshot shows local time. A line you saw at 19:30 in London in summer is 18:30 in the file. The four formats, using the same three lines from an invented session that began at 18:30:00 UTC:

For reading and for pasting into a show report. One line each: the time (UTC, to the second), the channel, the text. [18:30:07] Stage Manager: Front of house has cleared us, the house is yours. [18:30:21] Show Caller: Lighting cue 42, go. [18:31:02] Stage Manager: House open

For a spreadsheet. The first row names the columns: time,channel,speaker,kind,text. time,channel,speaker,kind,text 2026-11-16T18:30:07.412Z,Stage Manager,,speech,"Front of house has cleared us, the house is yours." 2026-11-16T18:30:21.090Z,Show Caller,,speech,"Lighting cue 42, go." 2026-11-16T18:31:02.655Z,Stage Manager,Ana,typed,House open Column What is in it time When the line started, as a full date and time in UTC, to the millisecond. channel The channel's name. speaker For a typed line, the name of whoever typed it. For a spoken line that Earshot put a name to, the id that person has in the show, not their name. Empty otherwise. kind speech, typed, or system (a notice Earshot wrote itself). text The line. It is wrapped in quotation marks when it contains a comma, a quotation mark or a line break.

Subtitle format, for laying the transcript against a video recording of the show. Times count from the start of the session, not from the clock. 1 00:00:07,412 --> 00:00:10,980 Stage Manager: Front of house has cleared us, the house is yours. 2 00:00:21,090 --> 00:00:22,870 Show Caller: Lighting cue 42, go. 3 00:01:02,655 --> 00:01:04,655 Stage Manager: House open Each entry runs from when the person started to when they stopped. A line with no length, such as a typed line, is given 2 seconds. To line it up with a video, you need to know how far into the session the recording started.

For other software. It is a list of every line with everything Earshot stored about it. [ { "id": "01KA4T8E2Y6ZB4N9Q7R1S3T5VX", "session_id": "01KA4T7Q9D5XJ2R8M3N6P0V1WC", "channel_id": "01KA2M5H8K0C3F6J9P2S5V8Y1B", "started_at": 1794853821090, "ended_at": 1794853822870, "text": "Lighting cue 42, go.", "raw_text": "Lighting Q42, go.", "words": [ { "text": "Lighting", "confidence": 0.98, "t0_ms": 0, "t1_ms": 420 }, { "text": "cue", "confidence": 0.91, "t0_ms": 480, "t1_ms": 700 } ], "language": "en", "speaker_id": null, "kind": "speech", "author": null, "keyword_hits": [], "has_clip": true, "latency_ms": 1040, "confidence": 0.94, "translations": {} } ] An invented line, shortened: a real one lists every word. The ids are made up. Field What it is id, session_id, channel_id Ids of the line, its session and its channel. The channel is an id here, not a name. started_at, ended_at When the person started and stopped, in milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC. text The line as saved. raw_text What the recogniser heard, when that differs from text. Otherwise null. For anyone below operator it is always null. words Each word with how sure Earshot was (0 to 1) and where it falls in the line, in milliseconds from the line's start. language The language of the line, when known. speaker_id The id of the person Earshot recognised, or null. kind speech, typed or system. author Who typed it, for a typed line. keyword_hits Where an automation's phrase matched in the text. has_clip Whether saved audio exists for the line. The audio itself is not in the export. latency_ms How long after the person stopped the final text was ready. confidence How sure Earshot was of the whole line (0 to 1), when known. translations Any translations made of the line, by language code. JSON is the only format that carries what was heard (raw_text). The others never do.
The same export is available from the host's web address, for a script that files the show report every night. See The API.

The production manager wants every call the show caller and stage manager made last night, as a spreadsheet, and wants to know when the interval began. Open Archive. Pick last night's session from the list. Under Markers, press Interval. The transcript jumps there, and the marker's time is the answer. Press the Show Caller chip, then the Stage Manager chip. Press Export, which now reads "Export (2 ch)", and choose CSV. Open the file in a spreadsheet. Remember the times are UTC. To find every time a particular cue was mentioned in the whole run, type cue 42 in Search what was said and press All sessions.
documents.s: A worked example: last night's show report

documents.t: There is no button for deleting past sessions in this build. How to start a fresh history by hand is in Privacy. Anyone who can connect can read the Archive and export it. In Open mode that is everyone on the network. See Who can connect. Anything said while the host was not running was not written down. Clearing a channel's transcript removes its lines, and makes their saved audio unreachable at once. See Replay a line's audio.
Replay a line's audio: the play control works in the Archive too Show files for New session… Where data and files live

The display button in the header (the "Aa" at the far right) opens Display on this device. It holds everything about how Earshot looks and reads on the screen in front of you: the language you read in, the theme, the text size, personal keyword alerts, and whether new lines are read aloud by a screen reader. Every role can change these. They are saved in your browser only. Nothing here changes the show, the host, or anyone else's screen, and a phone and a laptop each keep their own. The mock show "Spring Tour at Harbour Hall". Not a real show.

Read in chooses the language you read the transcript in: Original, or one of the languages the host can translate into, such as "español (Spanish)". While a language is on, the display button shows its code (for example ES). There is a lot to know about translation, starting with the fact that it is a reading aid and never a cue call. It has its own page: Read in another language.

Theme When to use it Dark The default. For a dark auditorium, a prompt desk, backstage. Light For a bright office, daylight load-ins, or printing a screenshot. High contrast Stronger edges and brighter text. For a dim screen seen from a distance, a washed-out monitor, or low vision. Light theme, mock show. Not a real show. High contrast theme, mock show. Not a real show. Channel colours, the red ARMED band and the Safe control keep their meaning in every theme. Nothing in Earshot relies on colour alone: Armed says "ARMED", a draft line is announced as "still speaking", and words Earshot was unsure of are underlined as well as dimmed.

Text size goes from 85% to 175%, in steps of 10. Press the minus and plus buttons (Smaller text, Larger text). The number between them is the size now. Reset returns to 100%. It scales the whole of Earshot on this device, and it scales Focus on top of Focus's own very large type. A console can also nudge the text size with OSC "font up" and "font down" messages. Those change the host computer's own window only, never a phone or another computer. See OSC addresses.

With Read new lines to screen readers ticked, each new finished line is announced to assistive technology as it arrives. It is on to begin with. Only finished lines are announced, never drafts as they change. Announcements are made while the Feed is open. On a busy show Earshot does not flood the reader: when more than three lines are waiting, it says how many new lines there are instead of reading each one. When you read in another language, the translation is announced, or the original if no translation arrived in time. Never both. If it is still too much to listen to, untick it. The transcript is there to move through at your own pace, and each line is labelled with its channel, the person's name if it has one, and its time.
documents.s: Read new lines to screen readers

documents.t: Turn on Flash when my name or keywords are mentioned, then enter your name or phrases in My name or keywords, separated with commas. For example: Jayden, lighting, standby sound. New spoken or typed lines on your selected channels trigger a five-second banner and a slow flash around the screen. The banner shows the matching keyword, channel and full line for context. Matching ignores case and punctuation and uses whole words: Ann does not match Annette. Drafts, system messages and loaded history do not trigger alerts. These alerts work while the show is Safe and need no automation. The settings stay in this browser and only this device flashes. Dismiss clears your alert; it does not affect anyone else. With reduced motion enabled on your device, the alert stays steady. A personal keyword alert in the mock show. Not a real show.
The What’s new in Earshot link opens the changelog in a new tab. It lists changes in each release, newest first.

Under the display settings, a section headed This device appears when there is something to offer: Install app, where the browser can install Earshot. See Installing on a phone. Sign out, for people who signed in with the show password. It asks "Sign out?" and warns "You'll need the password again to rejoin." On a phone the same two are also under More.
documents.s: This device: Install app and Sign out

documents.t: The stage manager's laptop at the prompt desk: Dark, text at 100%. The wall screen in the green room, showing Focus on Show Caller: High contrast, text at 150% so it reads from the sofa. A Spanish-speaking follow-spot operator's phone: Dark, text at 115%, Read in set to "español (Spanish)". Each was set on that device, once. None of them affects the others, and each is still set the next time that browser opens Earshot.
documents.s: A worked example: one show, three screens

documents.t: The settings live in the browser's storage for the address you opened. Opening Earshot by a different address, in a different browser, or in a private window starts from the defaults. So does clearing the browser's site data. On an iPhone, the Home Screen app and Safari are separate. Signing in on Safari does not carry over to the Home Screen app, so expect to set it up again there. Lane layouts and the Feed's channel filter are kept the same way. See Lanes and Feed.
Read in another language Focus The screen at a glance

The Feed is one merged timeline of every channel, newest at the bottom. It is the view most people leave open during a show. Each line shows the channel name in its colour, the time, and the text. Every role can read the Feed and type into channels that allow it. The mock show "Spring Tour at Harbour Hall". Invented lines, not a real show.

The summary line above the transcript says what you are looking at: "All channels", the names of one or two channels ("Show Caller and Stage Manager"), or a count ("4 of 8 channels"). The transcript in the middle. What each mark on a line means is in The screen at a glance. Channels, the panel on the right. On a narrow screen it is hidden behind a Channels button. The typing box along the bottom.

The Channels panel lists every channel under its group, each with a level meter, and a badge if something needs a look. A channel that belongs to no group is listed under "Other channels". Press a channel. The Feed now shows only that channel. Press another channel to add it. Press a selected channel again to take it out. Press a group's name (for example Stage) to add all its channels at once. Press it again to take them all out. Press Show all to clear the filter. Channels you have filtered out are dimmed in the list. They are still being transcribed, and you can still see their meters. The mock show, filtered to the Stage group: the summary reads "4 of 8 channels". Not a real show. info "Filtering changes this screen only. Groups are edited in Setup." Choosing channels here never changes a group, never changes what anyone else sees, and is never sent to the host. It is kept in this browser, so it is still there when you come back. On a phone, press Channels above the transcript to open the list. While a filter is on, the button reads Filter on, so you can tell at a glance that you are not seeing everything. The mock show on a phone-sized screen. Not a real show.

The Feed follows the newest line. Scroll up to read back, and it stops following so the text does not move under your eyes. While you are scrolled up, a Back to live button appears. It jumps to the newest line. If lines arrived meanwhile it also says how many, for example "Back to live 12 new". Lines older than what is loaded are fetched as you scroll up.
documents.s: Reading back, and getting back to live

documents.t: A channel in the list shows a count of lines you have not seen yet. This happens while you are scrolled up, or while the channel is filtered out. When a filter hides channels that have new lines, the summary line adds, for example, "7 new on hidden channels". Going back to live marks the channels you can see as read. A console can also clear the counts with an OSC "mark read" message. That works on the host computer's own window only. See OSC addresses.

Typed lines are for things that need writing down but were not said on comms: "House open", "Hold: medical in row F". In the box at the bottom, pick the channel. The placeholder then reads "Type to" and the channel's name. Type the line. It can be up to 500 characters. Press Send. The line appears in that channel with a Typed badge and the name of whoever sent it. The mock show, filtered to Stage Manager, just after typing a line. Your own lines show "You". Not a real show. A channel that does not accept typing is listed as, for example, "Video (no typing)". If you pick it, the box reads "Typing is off for this channel" and a note says "Video doesn't accept typed messages. Pick another channel." An admin sets this per channel with Allow typed messages (see Channel settings). Narrowing the Feed to a single channel also points the typing box at that channel. Nobody can type into a channel that comes from another Earshot computer. Those are read-only. If a line cannot be sent you see "The message was not sent. Check the connection and try again." warning Typed lines never fire phrase automations, whoever types them and whatever they say. Typing "go cue 42" sends nothing. That is deliberate: only speech fires a phrase automation. See Triggers. The name shown beside a typed line is the name the person gave when they joined, or the label on their personal link. It is a label, not proof of who they are.

You are the deputy stage manager on the mock show and you only care about the deck for the next ten minutes. In Channels, press Stage. The summary changes to "4 of 8 channels": Show Caller, Stage Manager, Deck Left and Deck Right. Deck Right is chatty and you do not need it. Press Deck Right. The summary now reads "3 of 8 channels". Lighting carries on talking. The summary shows "3 new on hidden channels", and Lighting shows a count of 3 in the list. Nothing is lost: it is all still being written down. Someone asks what the call was two minutes ago. Scroll up and read it. Back to live appears, and counts the new lines while you read. Press Back to live. Type a note for the record: pick Stage Manager in the box, type Scene change complete, 1 min 40, press Send. It appears with Typed and your name. When the change is done, press Show all. None of this changed what the lighting operator sees on their own screen.
documents.s: A worked example: following the stage during a scene change

documents.t: The Feed shows the current session. Earlier sessions are in the Archive. Filtering, text size and theme are per browser. A phone and a laptop each keep their own. A screen that drops off the network catches up on the lines it missed when it reconnects. Anything said while the host was down was not written down. See When the host restarts.
The screen at a glance for what each mark on a line means Lanes for the same lines as side-by-side columns Groups for making the groups you filter by Read in another language

Focus shows one channel, or one group, in very large type. It is made for a second screen: a monitor at the prompt desk, a display in the quick-change area, a screen beside the sound desk for someone who cannot wear a headset. Every role can use Focus. The mock show "Spring Tour at Harbour Hall". Invented lines, not a real show.

Open Focus. It starts on the first channel of the show. Use the box at the top left to choose. It lists Channels, then Groups. A channel shows only that channel's lines. The channel name is not repeated on every line, because it is in the box. A group merges the lines of the group's channels, and each line says which channel it came from. Until something is said, the screen reads "Waiting for" and the name. The top bar also carries the channel's level meter, its badge if it needs a look, and the Cloud mark if the channel is set to cloud speech. Each choice has its own address, so a screen can be set to open straight on it. For a channel the address ends #/focus/c/ followed by the channel's short name, for example #/focus/c/show-caller. Bookmark it on the machine that drives the second screen. If the channel is later deleted or its short name changes, the screen says "That channel was not found in this show. Choose another from the list."

The type is sized to the window: a bigger window gives bigger type. Your Text size setting (Display on this device) scales it further, from 85% to 175%. Draft lines are grey and final lines are solid, as everywhere else. Focus keeps the newest lines on screen (the last six finished lines, and whatever is being said now) and lets older ones go. It is for the call that is happening now. To read back, use the Feed or Lanes.

Button What it does Pop out Opens this Focus in its own window, without the rest of Earshot around it. Drag that window to the second screen. Keep on top In the desktop app's pop-out window only. The desktop app opens a pop-out already kept above other windows, so the button starts switched on. Press it to let other windows cover it. Full screen Fills the screen. Press it again (Exit full screen), or press Esc, to come back. It is offered only where the browser allows full screen. In a browser, Pop out opens a new browser window. If the browser blocks it you see "The pop-out window was blocked. Allow pop-ups for this page and try again." The new window is signed in as you are. You can also get to Focus from Lanes: a lane's menu has Pop out to Focus. warning In the desktop app, pop-out windows and Keep on top have not been tried by hand in this build. Try them on your own machine before you rely on them for a show. See Limits and known behaviour.
documents.s: Pop out, Keep on top, Full screen

documents.t: The dressers on the mock show need to see the show caller's calls and cannot wear headsets. On the laptop that drives the quick-change room's screen, open the address the operator gave you (see Who can connect). Open Focus and choose Show Caller. Press Pop out, drag the new window to the big screen, and press Full screen. Open the display button and raise Text size until the calls can be read from the far wall. On that laptop, switch off sleep and the screen saver. If the laptop sleeps, the screen stops updating. To show the whole deck instead, choose the Stage group in step 2. Each line then carries its channel name.
documents.s: A worked example: a call screen in the quick-change room

documents.t: A lighting desk or controller can change what the host computer's own window shows, with OSC: select a channel by name, step to the next or previous channel, scroll. Selecting a channel while the host's window is on the Feed (with all channels showing) or on Lanes switches it to Focus on that channel. These messages only ever move the Earshot window on the host computer itself. They are never sent to phones, tablets or other computers, and they do nothing while someone at the host is in Setup, Automations, Archive or Activity. See OSC addresses.

Focus shows live lines from the current session. To read an earlier session, use the Archive. Focus is for reading. To type a line, use the Feed. A screen is only as awake as its computer. Earshot cannot stop a laptop sleeping.
Lanes Display on this device Read in another language: Focus is one of the three views that translate

Lanes puts each channel in its own column, side by side, like the strips on a console. Use it when you need to follow several conversations at once without them interleaving, for example the show caller in one column and each deck in its own. Every role can use Lanes. How you arrange them is yours alone: it is saved in the browser you are using and changes nothing for anyone else. The mock show "Spring Tour at Harbour Hall", by channel. Invented lines, not a real show.

The header: the lane's name in its colour, a level meter, a badge if the channel needs a look, a count of new lines, and Speaking now while someone on it is talking. The lines, newest at the bottom. In each lane the time, and the person's name if there is one, sit on a row above the text, so the text gets the lane's full width. Load earlier lines at the top of a lane fetches older lines for that lane. Scroll a lane up to read back. A Live button in that lane takes it back to the newest line. Each lane scrolls on its own. The pencil and the play control work here exactly as in the Feed. See The screen at a glance.

At the top left, choose: By channel: one lane per channel. By group: one lane per group. Each lane merges the lines of that group's channels, and each line shows which channel it came from. The mock show by group. Not a real show. By group needs groups. If the show has none, the screen says "This show has no groups yet. Groups are made in Setup." An admin makes them: see Groups. Each of the two has its own layout. Hiding a lane in By channel does not hide anything in By group.

Beside the count of lanes ("8 of 8 lanes") is Arrange lanes. It opens a list of every lane. The Arrange lanes box on the mock show. Not a real show. For each lane you can: To do this In Arrange lanes Or from the lane's own menu Hide a lane Untick it Hide lane Show it again Tick it (a hidden lane has no menu) Pin it so it stays at the left while the others scroll sideways Press its pin Pin to the left, later Unpin Change the order The up and down arrows Move left, Move right, or drag the lane's header Open it large Pop out to Focus Pinned lanes are always first. A lane moves only among its own kind: pinned lanes among pinned lanes, the rest among the rest. The count beside the button keeps you honest: "5 of 8 lanes" means three are hidden, and it adds how many are pinned. Reset this layout puts the lanes back in show order, all showing, none pinned. Press Done to close the box. The box says it plainly: "Saved in this browser only. It does not change groups or what anyone else sees." If every lane is hidden the screen says "Every lane is hidden." Open Arrange lanes and tick one.

A phone shows one lane at a time, with the lane names as tabs across the top. Swipe sideways, or press a tab, to change lane. The first time, a hint says "Swipe sideways or use the tabs to change lane". A tab shows a count when its lane has new lines, and a dot while someone on it is speaking. The button at the right end of the tabs is Arrange lanes. The mock show on a phone-sized screen. Not a real show, and not tried on a real phone.

You mix front of house on the mock show. You want the show caller always in view, your own two channels next to it, and nothing from the deck. Open Lanes and choose By channel. Open the Show Caller lane's menu and choose Pin to the left. It now stays put when you scroll sideways. Open Arrange lanes. Untick Deck Left, Deck Right and Video. Use the arrows to move FOH Audio and Monitors to the top of the unpinned lanes. Press Done. The count reads "5 of 8 lanes, 1 pinned". The stage manager, on another laptop, still sees all eight lanes in show order.
documents.s: A worked example: a sound operator's layout

documents.t: A lane layout belongs to one browser on one device. It does not follow you to another device, and clearing the browser's site data loses it. A console's OSC "select channel" message, when the host's own window is on Lanes, switches that window to Focus on the channel. It never moves another device's screen. See OSC addresses.
Feed for everything in one timeline Focus for one channel in very large type Groups

Everything Earshot hears ends up as lines of text. This page explains the parts of the screen that are the same wherever you are: the views, the header, and what each mark on a line means. The pages after it take the views one at a time. Every role can read. Viewers, operators and admins all see the Feed, Lanes, Focus, the Archive and Activity. What differs is what each may do. See Roles. The mock show "Spring Tour at Harbour Hall". The lines are invented. It is not a real show.

The views are along the top of the screen. View What it is for Feed One merged timeline of every channel, newest at the bottom. Lanes One column per channel or group, side by side. Focus One channel or group in very large type, for a second screen. Archive Past sessions, search, markers and export. Automations Build, test and run automations. See Safe and Armed. Activity The live log of OSC, MIDI, web requests and automations. See Testing. Setup Devices, channels, groups, models and access. Admins only. On a phone the views are along the bottom instead: Feed, Lanes, Focus, Archive and More. More holds Automations, Activity, Setup, the API reference, and (where they apply) Install app and Sign out. The mock show on a phone-sized screen. Not a real show, and not a real phone: Earshot has not yet been tried on real phones or tablets.

From left to right: The show name. Check it is the show you expect. The connection indicator. It tells you whether this screen is hearing from the host. It says What it means Live Connected. New lines arrive as they are spoken. Connecting The page has just opened and is reaching the host. Reconnecting "Connection lost. Reconnecting (attempt N)." The screen keeps trying by itself. Engine unreachable "No connection to the engine. Retrying (attempt N)." Check the network, and that the host is running and awake. Demo Connected, but to a demo show, not a real one. Either the host was started in demo mode ("The engine is running its demo show.") or the page is using the built-in mock ("Showing the built-in demo show, not a live engine."). Safe or ARMED. Whether automations may send cues. Operators and admins get the control. Viewers see the state only. This is the most important control in Earshot: read Safe and Armed before a show. Safe. From the mock show. Armed. From the mock show: nothing was sent anywhere. The display button (the "Aa" at the far right). It opens Display on this device: theme, text size, and the language you read in. See Display on this device. When the show is Armed, a red band runs across the header and the browser tab title says "ARMED". The mock show, armed. Not a real show.

Each line is one stretch of speech (or one typed message) on one channel. Part What it tells you Channel name, in the channel's colour, with a strip of the same colour down the left edge Where it was said. Time When the person started speaking, in this device's local time. The text What Earshot heard. A person's name with a coloured dot, after the time Earshot recognised the voice. See "Names on lines" below. Typed badge, with a name Someone typed this line. It was not spoken. A small pencil at the right The text was changed from what the recogniser heard. See below. A small play control at the right The audio behind this line was saved and can be replayed. See Replay a line's audio. A link mark beside the channel name The channel comes from another Earshot computer. Hovering says "From" and that computer's address. See Showing another Earshot computer's channels. Lines Earshot writes itself (for example "Audio dropped out for 240 ms") appear in the channel they concern, set apart from speech.

A draft line is soft grey. The person is still talking, and the words can change as more audio arrives. A final line is solid. The person has stopped and Earshot has settled the text. In a final line, words Earshot was unsure of are dimmed and have a dotted underline. Read those words with care. Drafts appear only on channels where Show words as they are spoken is on (Setup, Channels), and only while Earshot is keeping up. In the first picture on this page, the grey lines at the bottom, which trail off in "…", are drafts. Three things wait for the final line: Cues set to fire on Final text (the recommended setting). See Building an automation. Glossary corrections. Draft text on screen is always as heard. Names on lines, the pencil and the play control.

On a channel with Separate and recognise voices on this channel on, a line can carry the name of the person Earshot recognised, in that person's colour. In the first picture, the Deck Left line carries the name Priya. The name arrives a moment after the line, never before it. Its text alternative is "Recognised by voice. May be wrong." Treat it as a reading aid. Short lines ("go", "copy") usually get no name. Every role sees names. Setting this up, and how often names are right, is in People: recognise voices.

A line that was changed from what the recogniser heard has a small pencil. The change can be: a glossary spelling ("aleesha" became "Alesha"), a number tidied up ("Q42" became "cue 42"), or a show word ("stand by" became "standby"). Press the pencil ("Changed from what was heard. Show the original.") and a small note headed Heard shows the original words. Hovering the pencil shows the same thing. The mock show in Lanes. The glossary corrected two words in this Lighting line, and the note shows what was heard. Not a real show. The changed text is what is saved, searched and exported. Only operators and admins see the pencil. In an Open show, and with the shared password, everyone is an operator, so everyone sees it. A personal-link viewer is never sent the original, and sees no pencil. A channel with Filter profanity on never shows a pencil, because the original would show the words the filter hid. The pencil and the play control sit together at the right of the line. They never change how tall a line is. info Automations hear what was said, not the corrected text. If a cue depends on a word that is often mis-heard, the pencil is how you find out what the recogniser actually wrote. See The glossary.

A channel set to cloud speech carries a small cloud mark in the channel list (in the pictures on this page, FOH Audio). It reads Cloud, Cloud paused or On this computer. It is there so nobody is surprised that a channel's audio may leave the building. What each wording means is in Badges, marks and indicators, and the feature itself is in Cloud & audio.

A channel that is listening normally shows no badge, only its level meter. A badge appears when something needs a look: Idle, Starting, Paused, Behind, No input, Offline or Error. Hover a badge for the detail. The full list is in Badges, marks and indicators. Behind is the one you will meet most. Hovering it says "Transcription is running behind; live drafts are paused until it catches up". Every line is still transcribed. Draft text stops, and final lines arrive later than usual. It comes on when the backlog on that channel goes over 3 seconds, and goes off when it falls under 1 second. Cues set to fire on final text fire later while a channel is Behind. No names appear on lines while a channel is Behind. If a gap appears in the audio, Earshot writes a line in the feed ("Audio dropped out for 240 ms") instead of hiding it. What to do about it is in Troubleshooting.

Open the first picture on this page again and read it from the top. The header says Spring Tour at Harbour Hall, Demo and Safe. So this is a demo show, the screen is connected, and no cue can be sent. "All channels" above the lines means nothing is filtered. The channel list on the right shows three groups: Stage (4 channels), Audio (2) and Lighting & Video (2). A Deck Left line carries Priya after its time. Deck Left has voice recognition on, and Earshot thinks it was Priya. It may be wrong. The Show Caller line "Warning on the house-out sequence, about two minutes." has a play control at its right edge. Show Caller keeps its audio, so you could replay that call. The lines at the bottom are grey and trail off. Those people are still talking. FOH Audio has a Cloud mark. That channel is set to cloud speech.
documents.s: A worked example: reading one minute of the mock show

documents.t: Earshot has been run with computer-made voices and a built-in microphone. Accuracy in a loud venue is unverified. Treat every line as something to confirm, and every cue more so. The screens have not been tried on real phones or tablets. See Limits and known behaviour.
Feed, Lanes, Focus, Archive Display on this device and Read in another language Badges, marks and indicators Words used in this manual

Earshot normally turns audio into text and keeps only the text. A channel can instead keep the audio behind each spoken line, so a call can be played back: "what exactly did the show caller say there?". The audio is saved on the host computer and nowhere else. It is off for every channel until an admin switches it on for that channel. info Who can do what. An admin switches saving on, per channel, and sets the limits. After that, anyone who can read the channel can replay it, viewers included.

Open Setup, then Channels, and choose the channel. Switch on Keep audio for replay. The app says: "Saves the audio behind each line on the host computer so anyone who can read this channel can replay it." Press Save changes. Only lines spoken after you switch it on have audio. Lines from before have none. Think about who is on the channel before you do this. Saved audio is a recording of people's voices. Tell the crew, and see Privacy.
documents.s: Switch it on for a channel

documents.t: A line from a channel that keeps audio gets a small play control at its right edge. Its name is "Play the audio of" followed by the channel and the time, for example "Play the audio of Show Caller, 19:42:07". It appears a moment after the line, because the audio is saved after the line is written. It works in Feed, Lanes, Focus and the Archive. Press it to play. Press it again to pause ("Pause the audio of…"), and again to carry on ("Resume the audio of…"). One line plays at a time. Starting another stops the first. The sound comes out of the device you pressed it on, not out of the host. In the picture below, the Show Caller and Stage Manager channels keep audio. Their lines have the control at the right edge. The other channels' lines do not. The mock show "Spring Tour at Harbour Hall". Invented lines. The mock has no real audio behind them. Not a real show.

The line Why A typed line It was never audio. A line from a channel with Keep audio for replay off Nothing was saved. A line spoken before the switch was turned on Nothing was saved then. A line from another Earshot computer (a linked channel) Only text crosses a link, never audio. A draft line The control comes with the finished line.

The control says What happened "This audio is no longer kept." The limits below deleted it, or the transcript was cleared. "This audio could not be loaded." The device could not fetch it. Check the connection and try again. "This audio could not be played." The device fetched it but could not play it.

Open Setup, then Cloud & audio, and find Saved audio. Two limits apply to all channels together: Setting Starts at Meaning Keep for (days) 14 Clips older than this are deleted. 0 means no age limit. At most (MB) 2048 The most disk space clips may use. When the total is over, the oldest go first. 0 means no size limit. Type the numbers and press Save. The limits are checked when Earshot starts, every 10 minutes, when you change them, and as clips are added. The clips live in the clips folder inside Earshot's data folder on the host. See Where data and files live. With both limits at 0, clips are kept until you clear the transcript or delete the folder. On a long run that can fill the disk.

Clearing a transcript makes its audio unreachable at once, and deletes the files. A clip that finishes being written after its line was cleared is deleted and never offered. An automation can clear a transcript, and so can a console at the Full control level. See Actions and OSC addresses.

After the mock show's first preview, lighting and the show caller disagree about what was called at the top of act two. Before the show, the admin opened Setup, Channels, Show Caller, switched on Keep audio for replay and saved. Under Cloud & audio the limits were left at 14 days and 2048 MB. After the show: Open Archive and pick tonight's session. Type act two in Search what was said. Press the matching Show Caller line. Press its play control and listen. Play the lines either side of it, one at a time. The lighting operator, who is a viewer on a personal link, can do exactly the same from their own phone.
documents.s: A worked example: checking a disputed call

documents.t: Replay was checked against the real host, but nobody has yet confirmed that it is audible on a phone or tablet speaker. Try it on the devices your crew will use. Only finished spoken lines have audio. There is no continuous recording: what falls between lines is not kept. The app has no button for saving a line's audio as a file. Saved audio is never sent to another Earshot computer, and is never part of a show file or a transcript export.
Channel settings for Keep audio for replay Cloud & audio for the Saved audio limits Privacy Archive, search and export

Each person can choose one language to read the transcript in. The lines are translated on the host and shown in that language, with the original underneath. It is set per device, so a Spanish-speaking crew member can read in Spanish while the stage manager beside them reads the original. danger Translation is a reading aid, never a cue call. Show jargon is often mistranslated. In testing, "Sound cue 7, go." came out in Spanish as "Suena a señal 7, vamos.", and "kick drum" as "tambor de patada". Do not call a cue, or act on one, from translated text. Read the original line beneath it. Every role can choose a language for themselves. Setting up what the host can translate into needs an admin.

Press the display button in the header (the "Aa"). It opens Display on this device. Under Read in, choose a language, for example "español (Spanish)". Original switches translation off. Close the menu. The display button now shows the language code (ES), so you can tell at a glance that you are reading a translation. "Lines show in this language, with the original beneath. Only for this device." Your choice is kept on this device. The first time a device opens a transcript view on a host that can translate, a hint under the header says "Read in another language: open Display", with Open Display and Dismiss. The mock show read in Spanish. The mock host does not really translate: some lines carry a stand-in "[es]" in front of the English. A real host shows a real translation there. Not a real show.

On the line What it means The translation, with Original and the original words beneath it The line was translated. The original, with Translating… beneath it The translation is on its way. It can take up to 10 seconds. The original, with Not translated beneath it No translation arrived in time, or the line is in a language Earshot cannot translate from. The line stays in the original. The line once, with nothing beneath The line is already in your language. Only finished lines are translated. A draft shows as heard until it settles. Only new lines are translated. Under the menu Earshot says: "Translating new lines into Spanish. Earlier lines may stay in their original language. Lines in a language Earshot cannot translate from stay in the original." Screen readers read the translation, or the original if none arrived in time, never both. Earshot holds the space for a translation before it arrives, so lines do not jump as you read.
documents.s: What you see on a line

documents.t: One language at a time for a viewer. Operators and admins can hold more, up to the host's limit. That limit is Languages at once under Setup, Cloud & audio. It starts at 4, and 0 turns translation off. Everyone's choices share it. Only while you are on Feed, Lanes or Focus does Earshot ask the host to translate for you. Lines that arrive while you are elsewhere (in the Archive, say) are not translated for you. The menu says so: "The host is asked while you are on Feed, Lanes or Focus." Automations never see a translation. They hear what was said. A cue cannot be fired, or missed, because of a translation.

Only languages the host can translate into: the target of each translation model installed on the host (pairs read "English to Spanish", so that one offers Spanish), or any common language, if the host uses a cloud translator. With nothing set up, the menu says "The host has no translation set up yet. An admin can add a translation model in Setup, under Models."
documents.s: Which languages appear in the menu

documents.t: The host can refuse a language. Earshot shows the host's own sentence. Under the header a bar reads, for example, "Can’t read in Italian." then the reason, then "Showing the original.", with Dismiss. In the display menu the same reason is followed by "Reading in the original." The two reasons you may see: The host says What to do "Nothing can translate into Italian here: install a translation model into Italian in Setup → Models, or set up a cloud translator." Ask an admin to install a pair that ends in that language, or to choose a cloud translator. "Only 4 languages can be translated at once (…)" Too many different languages are in use across the crew. Someone switches back to Original, or an admin raises Languages at once. If the host cannot be asked at all, you see "Could not ask the host about translation." and "Your language is kept, and Earshot will try again." Your choice is not lost.
There are two ways for a host to translate. Both are set on the host, not on the reader's device.

Text never leaves the host. Download pairs under Setup, Models. They are listed as pairs, "English to Spanish". See Models. German to English and English to Spanish have been run. German to Spanish works by way of English. Every other pair in the list is an untested download. Its description starts "Untested.". Each loaded pair uses about 330 MB of memory. Translation models have been built and run on an Apple Silicon Mac only.

Under Setup, Cloud & audio, Translate with has three cards: Card Where the text goes This computer (the default) Nowhere. Text never leaves. DeepL The text of each translated line goes to DeepL, outside the building. Needs a key. Claude The text of each translated line goes to Anthropic, outside the building. Needs a key. Choosing DeepL or Claude asks first ("Translate with DeepL?"). Audio is not sent, only the text of lines being translated. If DeepL fails, the models on this computer are used. Neither service has been tried with a real key in this build, so try one before you rely on it. A reader on a host that uses a cloud translator is told so in their own display menu: "The host sends the text of each line to DeepL to translate it." The keys, the confirmation and the status counters are described in Cloud & audio. What leaves the building, and when, is in Privacy.

The mock show's deck-right crew read Spanish more easily than English. The show is called in English. The admin, once, before the show: Setup, Models. Find the pair English to Spanish and press Download. This one has been run. Setup, Cloud & audio. Leave Translate with on This computer. Check Languages at once is at least 1. Each crew member, on their own phone: Open the display button. Under Read in choose "español (Spanish)". Go to Lanes or Feed. New lines appear in Spanish with Original and the English beneath. When the show caller says "Standby lighting cue 42", read the English line for the cue number. Trust the original for anything that matters. The stage manager's own screen is untouched: it still reads in the original.
documents.s: A worked example: a Spanish-speaking deck crew

documents.t: A reading aid, never a cue call. It bears repeating. A reader can pick a language that few lines can reach. The lines that cannot be translated stay in the original, and the host counts them as failed. Lines in a language Earshot cannot translate from stay in the original. Only the German to English and English to Spanish pairs have been run. DeepL and Claude have not been tried with a real key. See Limits and known behaviour.
Display on this device Models for downloading translation pairs Cloud & audio for Translate with and Languages at once Troubleshooting if lines are not translating

Find the heading that matches what you see, and go down its list in order. Each list starts with the most likely cause. What you see Go to No text on a channel No text is appearing A badge says Behind The badge says Behind You said the cue and nothing happened A cue did not fire A cue depends on a word Earshot gets wrong A cue depends on a word that is often mis-heard No names beside lines Names are not appearing on lines A name is spelled wrong every time A name keeps coming out wrong A channel from another Earshot computer is empty A linked channel shows no lines Lines stay in the original language Lines are not translating No play button on a line There is no play button on a line A phone or tablet will not connect A phone cannot connect A console sends OSC and nothing happens OSC is not arriving A MIDI controller does nothing MIDI is not triggering Two places to look first The header of every screen says whether the screen is Live and whether the show is Safe or ARMED. Activity says what every automation did, or why it did not. Most answers are in one of those two places.

Does the header indicator say Live? If not, the screen is not connected to the host. See A phone cannot connect. Is the channel enabled, and what does its badge say? No input, Offline, Error, Paused or Idle explain themselves. Hover the badge for the detail. See Status and badges. Is a speech model installed? Setup, Models should show Installed next to Parakeet and Silero VAD. See Models. Does the level meter move on that input? Look in Setup, Patch, or in the Channels list. If it does not move, the input number may be wrong, the device may not be delivering audio, or the operating system may have been denied microphone permission. Check the system's microphone permission for Earshot. See Patch and channels. Is the input too quiet? Raise Gain on the channel. If speech is still not picked up, look at Sensitivity under Advanced: speech detection. See Channels. Is the computer asleep? If the computer sleeps, Earshot stops listening.

Behind means transcription on that channel is running late. Every line is still transcribed. Draft text stops, and final lines arrive later than usual. It comes on when the backlog on that channel goes over 3 seconds, and goes off when it falls under 1 second. See Reading the transcript. To help it catch up: Turn off Show words as they are spoken on channels that do not need drafts. Drafts use more processing. Disable channels you are not using. Close other heavy programs on the host. Remember that cues set to fire on final text fire later while a channel is Behind.

Go down this list in order. Is the show Armed? In Safe nothing is sent. Open Activity: a row reading Would have fired Name with Dry run means it was matched and held back by Safe. See Safe and Armed. Was the show Armed from the moment the words began? Something said while the show is Safe never fires, even if you arm while Earshot is still working out the words. Activity says "heard before the show was armed" or "Safe was pressed after this was said". Arm first, then speak. Is the automation on, with no problem? Check the Enabled switch and look for a Problem badge or "1 automation is not running." See When an automation is not running. Did Earshot hear it correctly? Read the line in the Feed. Then type that line into the Test bench and see if the automation would fire. Remember it matches whole words, after numbers are turned into digits. See Run now, the Test bench and Activity. Was it refused for a number reason? Look in Activity for "Name" did not fire: the number may be incomplete: …. See How Earshot hears numbers, and say the number a different way. Cooldown. Activity says cooling down (N ms left). The default cooldown is 2 seconds. A condition. Activity says condition not met: …. Check channel, group, time window and flag conditions, and Where to listen. See Building an automation. The runaway stop. Look for the alert "fired 20 times in 10 seconds and was stopped". Was the line typed? Typed lines never fire phrase automations. Did it come from another Earshot computer? Lines from a linked channel never fire automations here. Is it limited to named people? It fires only when Earshot is very sure who spoke. Activity says why ("voice not recognised", "the voice was X, not Y", "no voice was heard for this trigger"). See Automations limited to people. Fire on Draft or Final. On Final text it waits for the settled line, and a channel that is Behind is slow. Did it fire, but the destination did not get it? Activity shows the send. A row marked Failed says why. Check the destination's host, port and protocol (under OSC destinations in the editor), and whether the device is on the network. A TCP destination that is down is retried, and the sends skipped meanwhile are logged. See Actions.

Automations hear what was said, not the corrected text. The glossary changes only what people read. Add the mis-hearing to the automation's phrases. For example, if you want "alesha go" to fire a cue but the recogniser writes "aleesha go", add "aleesha go" as another phrase in the automation. See Triggers and Glossary.
documents.s: A cue depends on a word that is often mis-heard

documents.t: Setup, Models: is Voice recognition (CAM++) installed? The People screen says if it is not. Setup, People: does the person show Voice learned? "No voice yet" or "Voice needs learning again" means learn it. Setup, Channels: is Separate and recognise voices on this channel on for that channel? New audio channels start with it on; existing channels keep their previous setting. Is the line very short? Short lines get no name. A line needs about a second of real speech. Is the channel Behind, or did the model only just start? Lines get no name then. The voice may not be learned, or not learned on this channel. A name can also be missing because Names on lines is on Cautious. See People.
documents.s: Names are not appearing on lines

documents.t: Add it to the glossary (Setup, Glossary) with the way it comes out under Sounds like. Look for "Not applied:" on the entry: Earshot will not apply a correction that touches a number or a word an automation listens for. See Glossary.
documents.s: A name keeps coming out wrong

documents.t: Read the status line under the channel. The status says What to do "Connecting to …" Wait. It is still trying. "Cannot reach …: … Retrying." The other computer is off, or the network between the two is down. Earshot keeps trying by itself. "The link code was refused. …" Save the channel again with the right code, or switch it off and on. A refused code is not retried, and fixing the code on the other computer alone does not bring the link back. "… refused the link: …" Check the other computer still has Shared with other Earshot hosts on for that channel. "Linked to …", but no lines Nobody has spoken on that channel since the link came up, or the channel is paused here. See Showing another Earshot computer's channels.
documents.s: A linked channel shows no lines

documents.t: Is a language chosen under Read in (the display button in the header)? Are you on Feed, Lanes or Focus? Earshot asks the host to translate for you only on those three. Does the menu offer the language? It lists only what the host can translate into. An admin needs to install a pair under Setup, Models, or choose a cloud translator. If the host refused, the sentence under the display menu (and the bar under the header) says why. A line that says Not translated was not translated in time, or is in a language Earshot cannot translate from. See Read in another language.

Only spoken lines from a channel with Keep audio for replay on get one, a moment after the line. Lines from before it was switched on have none. Typed lines have none. If it says "This audio is no longer kept.", the retention limits deleted it. See Replay a line's audio.
documents.s: There is no play button on a line

documents.t: What the phone shows What to do "This address isn't one the host recognises." Use the address under Setup, Access, Address for the crew. "Can't reach the Earshot computer. Check your network and try again." Check the phone is on the same network as the host. The page keeps trying by itself. The password page: "That password is not right." Check it. After five wrong tries a device is locked out: "Too many tries. Try again in m:ss." Wait. "This show needs a personal link or QR code from the operator." The show is on Personal links. Make the person a link or invite. "This code is not valid or has already been used. Ask the operator for a new one." An invite works once and lasts 10 minutes. Make a new one. Signed in on a Home Screen app on iPhone, but Safari was used before Sign-in does not carry over. Ask for a new code. Everyone was working, then everyone is sent to a sign-in page The password was changed, the access mode changed, or the host restarted. "Reconnecting" or "Engine unreachable" in the header The screen has lost the host. It keeps trying by itself. Check the host is running and awake. See Who can connect, Password, Invites and personal links, Phones and tablets and What happens when the host restarts.

Is Controllers may send OSC to Earshot on? New audio channels start with it on; existing channels keep their previous setting. Is the level high enough? Make safe only ignores everything except Safe, ping and version. Move to Trigger automations for triggers, or Full control to clear transcripts or arm. Is the sending device in Devices allowed to control? The list starts as "Only this computer". Add its IP address. For arming: it needs the level set to Full control, a TCP port set, and the sender connected by TCP. A UDP sender can never arm. Is the port right? UDP 4781 by default; TCP is empty until you set it. Look in Activity. Refused OSC is logged with the reason and a count. If you added a device list, is it a plain IP address (no port, range or name)? Is the address spelled exactly as in the address list? There are no aliases. Did a view control (select channel, scroll) do nothing? It only changes the Earshot window on the host computer, and not while someone is in Setup, Automations, Archive or Activity. Did an Arm do nothing? A packet that also contains a Safe never arms. Look in Activity for "Arm ignored". To prove the path, send /earshot/ping and wait for /earshot/reply/pong. It works from any device at every level. See OSC examples and OSC input.
